name: Agecroft Hall

dates.altered: The house is a re-erection, not a building: the nomination records that 'Williams had the building dismantled and brought parts of it back to Virginia' and that 'A l l four sides of the former quadrangle were not to be reproduced.' A new steel frame carries it.
dates.note: The National Register infobox gives 'Built 1926'; the style node's exemplar gives 1928; the nomination itself dates the purchase to 1925 and describes the house 'as i t stood i n 1925' in Lancashire. The English fabric is late-15th to late-16th century by the nomination's own account. Four dates for one building, and none of them is edited here.

refs.title: NOMINATION FORM ... Agecroft, Richmond, Virginia -- Virginia Historic Landmarks Commission Survey, December 1977
refs.note: The nomination's own description of the exterior, verbatim and OCR included: 'Agecroft consists of a two-and-one-half-story, stone-foundation, gable-roof manor house from which radiates a series of wings and dependencies. The exterior wall? of the complex are. finished i n a variety of decorative timber framing including omamental and herringbone paneling and small framing. Most of the a r c h i t e c t u r a l fragments found on both the i n t e r i o r and exterior of the house date from the l a t e 16th and 17th centuries. Between the exposed timbers i s rough-cast stucco which conceals a s t e e l frame. Casement windows of l a t t i c e d leaded glass are used throughout the building.' The nomination also records the architect as 'New York architect Homer G. Morse', where the Wikipedia infobox reads 'Henry G. Morse'; both are recorded and neither is corrected.

refs.title: Agecroft Hall - Wikipedia
refs.note: Gives the address as 4305 Sulgrave Road, Windsor Farms, and the architectural style as 'Tudor-Tudor Revival', which is the register's own two-word answer to the question this record exists to pose.

note: Written for WP-11.2 Tranche 2. This is the corpus's cleanest CONTROL for the revival's own claim, and the nomination hands it over in one sentence: 'Between the exposed timbers i s rough-cast stucco which conceals a s t e e l frame.' A genuine late-Tudor Lancashire house, shipped and re-erected in 1926 -- and the wall that reads as fifteenth-century framing is stucco over 1920s steel. tudor-revival's own description.long says the style's economics 'run exactly opposite to its imagery'; this building runs them opposite at the one place where the imagery was real. Immediately to the east is Virginia House, the same story told a second time by a different owner.
